subject: Rapid-start: TTFT & streaming criteria + demo request
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Ng <clara.ng@finosight.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T18:02:00Z
Subject: Rapid-start: TTFT & streaming criteria + demo request

Hi Clara —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from my side so we have aligned next steps and a concise checklist for the pilot: 

1) Performance targets you mentioned
   - Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: sub-150ms for initial chunk for interactive web chat (desktop + mobile)
   - Concurrency: target ~250 concurrent active sessions at peak
   - Typical prompt size: ~40–120 tokens preface + ~200 tokens completion on average

2) Streaming preferences
   - You prefer SSE for browser clients; WebSocket ok for mobile SDKs if we need bidirectional presence
   - Chunk cadence: you indicated a desire for more frequent partial updates — we recommend 50–100 token chunks with a max of 200ms pacing, but open to tuning based on UX tests

3) Throughput and reliability
   - Expected sustained throughput during peak: ~60k tokens/minute across the cluster (ballpark)
   - Fallback: graceful degrade to batched non-streaming responses for very long completions / when backend runs into capacity headroom

Next steps I propose:
- Vivek to draft a lightweight perf validation plan (small-scale load test for TTFT + chunk cadence) — target week of Oct 19
- Marissa to schedule a 30-minute demo + integration Q&A (customer-facing) — target this week if possible
- I’ll attach a draft SLA and a short runbook outlining the streaming test harness and sample metrics to capture (TTFT histogram, first-byte, chunk intervals)

Attachments: finosight-sla-draft-v1.pdf, rapidstart-streaming-runbook.xlsx

If that matches what you heard, I’ll queue up the test plan and propose two demo slots.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Clara Ng <clara.ng@finosight.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, procurement@finosight.com
Date: 2026-10-11T19:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Rapid-start: TTFT & streaming criteria + demo request

Thanks Jonas — this is great and matches what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side:

- TTFT: sub-150ms is ideal for the chat surface. We can tolerate up to 250ms intermittently but would like median to be under 120ms once tuned.
- Concurrency: 250 concurrent interactive sessions at global peak. We have unpredictable spikes (short bursts) so headroom for autoscale is important.
- Chunk cadence: user testing favors smaller early chunks (40–80 tokens) to give the feeling of responsiveness, then 100–150 token cadence for the steady-state. Latency on the first chunk feels most important for UX.

Regarding verification: we need a short live proof (15–20 min) showing typical session TTFT numbers from your hosted system, and a separate 1-hour smoke load test showing TTFT distribution at ~250 concurrency. Will your team run both or do you want us to run a synthetic runner?

Also copying procurement — they’ll want the SLA and a statement about data retention/audit logs for the pilot.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Clara
Clara Ng
Head of Product, FinoSight
clara.ng@finosight.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Ng <clara.ng@finosight.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Rapid-start: TTFT & streaming criteria + demo request

Clara —

Perfect, thanks for the specifics. Short answers and proposal below: 

Who runs verification
- Redwood can run the live 15–20 min demo from our hosted env (we’ll share a dashboard with TTFT/first-byte histograms). Vivek will own the demo instrumentation.
- For the 1-hour smoke test we can either: (a) run it from our dedicated test cluster against a representative workload, or (b) provide you a lightweight runner (Docker image + instructions) to run from your environment. I recommend Redwood-run test first so we can iterate quickly.

Technical test plan (summary)
- Goal: validate median TTFT < 120ms, 95th percentile < 250ms at 250 concurrent interactive sessions.
- Client transport: SSE for browser test; WebSocket runner for mobile path.
- Chunking: start with an initial small chunk of 48 tokens (aim for first-chunk < 120ms), then steady cadence of 96 tokens with a soft 150–200ms max inter-chunk window. We’ll record inter-chunk latency distribution.
- KV-cache warmup: we’ll run a warmup phase to prime common prompts; cold-start behavior will be included in a separate short run.
- Metrics captured: TTFT (ms), first-byte, chunk intervals (ms), tokens/sec per instance, error rate, tail latency.

Operational notes
- Autoscale headroom: suggest allowing a 1.5x headroom on provisioned concurrency for the pilot to avoid oscillation on short bursts.
- Fallback behavior: we’ll implement a server-side switch to fall back to batched completion (single response) after 1.5s of chunking if the model stalls.

Next steps
- Vivek will post a short runbook and a test slot for Oct 19–20 (proposed)
- I attached the initial SLA + runbook for your procurement team to review.
- Marissa will propose demo times and open the procurement/DocuSign thread.

Let us know if we should run the 1-hour smoke from our side — we’ll need a nominal API key and a small seed prompt corpus (we can use sanitized demos).

Thanks,
Jonas
